commit_dialog_autosave_note: Unsaved changes will be saved first.
commit_dialog_prefilled_note: Prefilled — overwrite it or just confirm as-is.
commit_nothing_to_commit: Nothing to commit — no changes since the last commit.
history_restore_hint: Loads into the editor for review — does not commit automatically.
restore_diff_intro: Differences from the current state — select what should be applied.
restore_confirm_summary: {{count}} changes will be applied. The server restarts briefly.
restore_confirm_snapshot_hint: A snapshot of the current state is created automatically before applying — reversible at any time.
restore_success_restart_hint: An addon restart is recommended so MQTT/webhooks fully pick up the restored configuration.
confirm_clear_logs: Do you really want to delete the entire server log?
blockly_no_trigger_warning: This script has no trigger block, so it will never actually run when enabled. Save anyway?
blockly_trigger_on_tooltip: Runs the attached actions whenever the entity's state changes, no matter what it changes to.
blockly_trigger_on_state_tooltip: Runs the attached actions only when the entity changes to this specific state.
blockly_on_webhook_tooltip: Runs the attached actions whenever an external service sends a request to this webhook's URL (shown in the Webhook Panel once saved). A secret token is generated and verified automatically — no extra setup needed for the common case. Use "webhook data" to read what was sent, and "respond to webhook" to send a reply (add one, or the request hangs until it times out). Advanced options (no-auth public endpoints, IP allowlists, signature verification, GET instead of POST) aren't available here — use "Duplicate as JavaScript" for those.
blockly_webhook_data_tooltip: The body of the request that triggered this webhook — only valid inside a "when webhook ... is called" block. Automatically parsed as JSON when possible.
blockly_webhook_respond_tooltip: Sends the reply back to whatever called this webhook — only valid inside a "when webhook ... is called" block. Add one at the end of your actions, or the caller waits until the request times out.
blockly_schedule_interval_tooltip: Runs the attached actions repeatedly, on a fixed interval.
blockly_schedule_daily_tooltip: Runs the attached actions once a day, at this time (24h clock).
blockly_schedule_cron_tooltip: Advanced: enter a cron expression (e.g. "0 8 * * *") or shorthand ("every 15m", "every weekday at 6:00", "every monday at 9:00"). An online cron expression generator can help build the raw form.
blockly_call_service_tooltip: Calls a Home Assistant service for the given entity. Click the gear icon to add extra data (brightness, temperature, ...); rename each field directly on the block.
blockly_log_tooltip: Writes a message to the script log at the chosen level. Plug in text, or something like "state of" to log a value.
blockly_stop_tooltip: Stops the current script. The reason (optional, can be left blank) shows up in the logs.
blockly_entity_tooltip: An entity ID, reusable in any of the sockets below. Picks from a live list of entities from Home Assistant.
blockly_get_state_tooltip: The current state of an entity, as text (e.g. "on", "off", "21.5"). Plug this into a comparison or another block.
blockly_get_attribute_tooltip: A specific attribute of an entity (e.g. "temperature" on a climate entity, "brightness" on a light).
blockly_time_since_tooltip: Milliseconds since the entity last changed. Leave "to" blank for the last change to any value; fill it in to instead find the last time it changed specifically to that state (e.g. "on").
blockly_trend_tooltip: Whether a numeric sensor is "rising", "falling", or "stable" over a time window (default 1 hour) — e.g. "1h", "30m", "2d". Leave blank for the default.
blockly_get_calendar_events_tooltip: Upcoming events on this calendar (default window: now through 7 days from now), as objects ({ summary, start, end, all_day, ... }).
blockly_get_todo_items_tooltip: All items on this todo list, as objects ({ uid, summary, status, ... }) — status is "needs_action" or "completed".
blockly_get_entities_in_area_tooltip: The entity IDs of everything assigned to this area (e.g. "everything in the living room"). Fetched once on startup — restart the script if area assignments change.
blockly_get_entities_with_label_tooltip: The entity IDs carrying this label. Fetched once on startup — restart the script if label assignments change.
blockly_get_areas_tooltip: The full list of areas registered in Home Assistant, as objects ({ area_id, name, ... }) — mainly useful for debugging (e.g. plug into "log") or counting with "length of". For working with the entities inside an area, use "entities in area" instead.
blockly_get_labels_tooltip: The full list of labels registered in Home Assistant, as objects ({ label_id, name, color }) — mainly useful for debugging (e.g. plug into "log") or counting with "length of". For working with the entities carrying a label, use "entities with label" instead.
blockly_wait_tooltip: Pauses the script for the given number of seconds before continuing.
blockly_wait_for_state_tooltip: Pauses until the entity's state becomes this value. Without a timeout, waits indefinitely and simply continues once reached. With a timeout, two branches appear: "on success" runs if the state was reached in time, "on timeout" runs if it wasn't — the wait itself never raises a script error in that case.
blockly_notify_tooltip: Sends a notification to your Home Assistant companion app. Title and target are optional (leave blank for the default). Check "show in Home Assistant" to show it in HA's own notification bell instead — works without a companion app, handy for testing.
blockly_ask_tooltip: Sends an actionable notification with buttons and waits for the user to tap one (requires the HA companion app — does not work in a web browser). Click the gear icon to add buttons — each gets its own "do" branch, run when tapped. Checking "use timeout" also reveals an "if no answer" branch, run if nothing is tapped in time.
blockly_register_tooltip: Creates a new Home Assistant entity (or updates its config if it already exists). Click the gear icon to add more options (unit, device class, area, ...).
blockly_update_tooltip: Updates the state of an entity previously created with "register entity". Click the gear icon to also set extra attributes.
blockly_store_get_tooltip: Reads a value from the global store (persists across restarts and is shared between scripts). Returns nothing (undefined) if the key was never set.
blockly_store_set_tooltip: Writes a value to the global store. Persists across script/addon restarts and is visible to other scripts under the same key. Check "secret" to mask the value in the Store Explorer UI.
blockly_store_delete_tooltip: Removes a key from the global store.
blockly_store_on_tooltip: Runs the attached actions whenever this store key's value changes — useful for reacting to a value another script wrote.
blockly_mqtt_subscribe_tooltip: Runs the attached actions whenever a message arrives on this MQTT topic. Wildcards + (single level) and # (multi-level, must be last) are supported. The message payload is available as "MQTT payload" inside this block.
blockly_mqtt_payload_tooltip: The payload of the MQTT message that triggered this block — only valid inside a "when MQTT message" block. Automatically parsed as JSON when possible, otherwise a plain string.
blockly_mqtt_publish_tooltip: Publishes a message to an MQTT topic. Objects are automatically sent as JSON. Check "retain" so new subscribers immediately get the last published value.
error_script_exists: A script with this name already exists.
warn_device_class_icon: Warning: Entity '{{entityId}}' uses device_class '{{deviceClass}}'. Home Assistant often ignores custom icons for these classes in favor of class-specific defaults.
library_mode_banner: LIBRARY MODE — This script is passive. Use @include {{filename}} in automations.
warn_library_in_use:
Warning: Library '{{filename}}' is used by {{count}} script(s): {{scripts}}.
Do you really want to delete it?
wizard_from_repo_intro: In Git, but no longer on disk:
wizard_from_repo_empty: No deleted scripts in the Git history.
wizard_duplicate_as_js: Duplicate as JavaScript (keeps the original .blocks script untouched)
wizard_type_tooltip:
Determines how the script is exposed to Home Assistant. This controls the @expose header inside the script's code.

- 'Switch': Creates an entity with on/off state (@expose: switch).
- 'Button': Creates a button to execute the script (@expose: button).
- 'Background': No visible entity in HA (no @expose).
- 'Library': Reusable code that can be imported by other scripts (no @expose).
wizard_dropzone_text: Drop file here or click to select
wizard_url_hint: The URL must point directly to the raw (.js) content.
wizard_import_warning: Warning: Only import code from trusted sources.
safe_mode_msg: Bootloop detected. All scripts have been stopped to protect the system.
safe_mode_deactivated: Safe Mode deactivated. You can now start scripts manually.
sibling_guard_msg: "{{sibling}}" is currently running. Both add-ons share the same scripts, data, and webhook port, so they must never run at the same time.
sibling_guard_hint: Stop "{{sibling}}" in the add-on view — this add-on will then activate automatically (checked every 15 seconds).

general.expert_mode_desc: Shows the developer toolkit: event inspector, live REPL, breakpoints, and more.
general.confirm_delete_desc: Shows a confirmation dialog before deleting scripts.
general.hide_mobile_toggle_in_desktop: Hide mobile toggle in desktop mode
general.hide_mobile_toggle_in_desktop_desc: Hides the mobile/desktop view switch button while in desktop mode. It always stays visible in mobile mode.

editor.word_wrap_desc: Word wrap can also be controlled via the button in the toolbar.

statusbar.show_statusbar_desc: Displays the status bar at the bottom of the application.
statusbar.show_sparkline_desc: Displays a small historical graph for this value.
statusbar.hide_sparkline_on_dense_desc: Automatically hides mini charts when all 3 slots are active. This prevents the status bar from looking cluttered or text being truncated.
statusbar.header_action_desc: HA entity to show as a quick-action button in the sidebar header (switch or button).
statusbar.git_no_remote: Git: local only (no GitHub remote configured)

mqtt.host_desc: Mosquitto addon: core-mosquitto | External broker: IP or hostname
mqtt.mqtt_autodetect_success: MQTT settings successfully imported from Home Assistant.
mqtt.mqtt_autodetect_not_found: No MQTT configuration found in Home Assistant.
mqtt.mqtt_autodetect_password_hint: Host and port have been imported. Please enter your password manually.
mqtt.mqtt_autodetect_fallback: No MQTT configuration found in HA – core-mosquitto suggested as default. Please enter your credentials manually.
mqtt.mosquitto_hint:
Mosquitto addon (HA): Use core-mosquitto as host.
The broker requires a real Home Assistant user for authentication.
Recommended: Create a dedicated MQTT user at Settings → People → Add User.

webhook.external_url_desc: Base URL shown in the Webhook Panel for copying (e.g. https://myha.example.com). Only needed behind a reverse proxy. The webhook server always listens on port 3001 (fixed, see add-on network configuration).
webhook.trust_proxy_desc: Reads the real caller IP from X-Forwarded-For. Only enable this when a trusted reverse proxy actually sits in front of the webhook port — otherwise callers can spoof their IP.

backup.schedule_enabled_desc: Runs on a schedule, server-side — no download needed.
backup.retention_count_desc: Number of backups to keep — older ones are deleted automatically. Applies to both local and WebDAV.
backup.webdav_enabled_desc: Uploads every backup there too, best-effort. The local copy stays authoritative if the upload fails.
backup.restore_open_desc: Rare, disaster-recovery tool — day-to-day single-file recovery is the script editor's History panel instead.

versioning.about_hint: Scripts are versioned automatically in a local Git repository (Commit button in the editor toolbar, History panel next to it). No account needed. A GitHub remote below is optional.
versioning.github_enabled_desc: Pushes every commit there too, best-effort — commit itself never depends on GitHub being reachable.
versioning.github_token_desc: GitHub PAT with repo write access. Same security level as the MQTT password, injected into the push URL per-request and never written to .git/config.
versioning.push_desc: Separate from Commit — a flaky GitHub connection never blocks committing. Pushes whatever's currently unpushed.

system.title: System Settings
system.default_throttle_desc: Delay between individual entities in ha.select() calls.
system.mqtt_autodetect_success: MQTT settings successfully imported from Home Assistant.
system.mqtt_autodetect_not_found: No MQTT configuration found in Home Assistant.
system.mqtt_warning_expose: Script uses @expose, but MQTT is not active.
system.mqtt_banner_disabled_desc: Enable MQTT in settings to expose your scripts to Home Assistant.
system.mqtt_banner_disconnected_desc: Connection to broker lost. Scripts might not be controllable in HA.

danger.node_memory_desc: Maximum RAM per script. Prevents a single script from crashing the system.
danger.restart_count_desc: Number of crashes within the time window before Safe Mode is activated.
danger.restart_time_desc: Period in seconds during which crashes are counted for bootloop detection.
danger.filesystem_enabled_desc: Grants scripts access to ha.fs for reading and writing files within sandboxed directories (/config/js_automations/data/, /share/, /media/). Use with caution.
danger.quota_desc: Maximum total size for this virtual root. 0 = unlimited.
danger.capability_enforcement_desc: When enabled, scripts that use network (http/https/fetch) or shell execution (child_process) without declaring @permission in their header will throw a PermissionDeniedError at runtime.
